items.title: Proper base change for the derived pushforward of a complex on topological spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)

items.difficulty_reason: In a cartesian square of topological spaces with the vertical map proper, the theorem shows that the base change map relating the inverse image of the derived pushforward to the derived pushforward of the inverse image is an isomorphism for every bounded below complex (statement lines 3100-3119). The proof is a reduction to the pointwise statement: it suffices to check the map on stalks, properness is preserved by base change and supplies the closedness, separatedness and quasi-compact fibre hypotheses needed to apply the fibre formula for stalks of higher direct images on both sides of the square, and the two sides are then identified because the induced map of fibres is a homeomorphism pulling one restriction back to the other (proof lines 3121-3139). The claim is H2: no new construction, but the verification that the hypotheses of the fibre formula hold on both sides of the square is what makes the reduction work.
